To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a generalization of the Independent pair model to nuclear states non-describable by a single configuration, and that the energy of the T=0, Jπ=0+ excited state of 4He was calculated with an approximate solution.

the generalized equations of the Independent pair Model are capable of reproducing the experimental excitation energy of the T=0,Jπ =0+ state of 4He, if the parameters of the model potential are determined from two-nuclear scattering data.
We have generalized the equations of the Independent-Pair Model for finite nuclei to nuclear states non-describable by a single-shell-model configuration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics: 1.
the application of the Independent Pair model to nuclear systems in which the shell model description is not applicable.
the development of a theory of the nucleus, which is based on the concept of independent nucleon pairs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the IP-model is able to describe the ground states of all light nuclei with the exception of4He and3H, and the excited states of all light and medium nuclei with the exception, perhaps, of the excitedT = 0, Jπ = 0+ -state in4He.
the generalized IP model, as presented in this thesis, provides a consistent and unified theoretical framework to describe the ground states and excited nuclear states of all finite nuclei.
the Independent Pair Model, as a model for nuclear ground states, has been confirmed to a high degree of accuracy by the experimental data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the generalizations of the Independent Pair model equations are a useful tool for the calculation of excited states of finite nuclei, and that the Independent Pair model is a useful model for the calculation of nuclear properties.
the Independent Pair Model can be applied to degenerate nuclear systems, if the degeneracy is not too large.

, in spite of the fact that the Independent Pair Model does not contain any adjustable parameters and that it is based on a very simple and crude approximation, it yields results which are comparable to the results of other more sophisticated methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy of the T=0, Jπ=0+ state in 4He is not sensitive to the details of the nucleon-nucleon interaction, but is mainly determined by the nuclear density distribution.
the energy of the T=0,Jπ = 0+ -state is not a very sensitive test for the validity of the Independent Pair model.

the Independent Pair Model, which is a very successful description of nuclear ground states, can be generalized to excited states, too, and that the model can be used as a starting point for a more sophisticated description of nuclear states.
